div.h1: As world heads for overshoot of 1.5°C, adaptation is too slow

img.alt: Four firefighters pose for a picture

h3.a: Climate technology is already changing lives. Why isn’t it reaching more people?

div.div: As climate change intensifies, technology is vital for protecting lives and livelihoods in the developing world, says Ariesta Ningrum, head of the UN’s Climate Technology Centre and Network.

h3.a: From ozone protection to sustainable cooling: shaping the next chapter

div.div: Elizabeth Mrema, UNEP Deputy Executive Director, said the Montreal Protocol proves world cooperation works, urging ambition, funding and action on sustainable cooling

img.alt: A closeup of a mobile phone

h3.a: What's inside the things you buy? How digital passports could help reveal the answer.

div.div: Digital product information systems can help make supply chains more transparent, giving companies the information they need to reduce hazardous chemicals and support circularity.

h3.a: UNEP Executive Director media statement for the Adaptation Gap Report 2026

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, says the world is not ready for worsening climate impacts and must rapidly scale adaptation finance to build resilience and save lives.

img.alt: Mangrove forest located in the Mida Creek - Malindi

h3.a: As world heads for overshoot of 1.5°C, adaptation is too slow

div.div: With global warming set to exceed 1.5°C, adaptation finance falls far short of needs, implementation is constrained by institutional barriers, and losses and damages are mounting, according to new report from the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).

h3.a: Is climate change propelling the rise of superbugs?

div.div: Experts fear climate change may be fueling the rise of superbugs, adding to a global crisis of antimicrobial resistance.

h3.a: UNEP Executive Director statement on the closing of COP17 in Yerevan, Armenia.

div.div: The world has already agreed a global plan to safeguard nature. This COP was about accelerating implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), and turning those targets into decisive, real-world action.

h3.a: Laying down the law on biodiversity

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, said courts and judges are vital to closing biodiversity implementation gaps and advancing environmental rule of law today.

h3.a: A new platform for healthy mountain ecosystems

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, called for global backing of the Yerevan Platform to protect mountain and freshwater ecosystems and boost biodiversity action.

img.alt: An aerial view of a fork in a river.

h3.a: Why nature-based solutions for cities are the future of urban resilience

div.div: Discover how 24 cities in 19 countries are using nature-based solutions to fight climate change, restore ecosystems and build urban resilience.

img.alt: Launch of the Model Framework Forest Act

h3.a: New model forest act can help halt and reverse deforestation

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, called for stronger laws and action to halt deforestation, keep forests standing and advance global biodiversity, climate and restoration goals.

h3.a: Nature is making a comeback, but the world must move faster to meet restoration targets – UN Report

div.div: A UN report published today finds that 252 million hectares (ha) across 149 countries are being restored, creating more than one million green jobs – the largest documented global restoration effort to date
Credit: Philippe Matheini and Michael Booth

h3.a: UN report shows nature is being restored at an unprecedented scale

div.div: The Restoration Progress Report: Nature’s Comeback, released on 29 October, says an area of land and sea the size of Kazakhstan is now being repaired.

img.alt: Aerial view of Anini and Kalihiwai beaches on the north coast of Kauai

h3.a: UN report urges investment in Ocean Carbon Intelligence to safeguard the ocean's climate role

div.div: The world must strengthen its understanding of the ocean's carbon system if it is to safeguard one of the planet's most important climate allies, according to the UN’s 2026 Climate Technology Progress Report released today.

h3.a: Armenia, in partnership with UNEP, launches global initiative to drive action on mountain and related freshwater ecosystems

div.div: The Republic of Armenia, in its capacity as Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) COP17 Presidency, in partnership with the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), launched a new initiative to accelerate global efforts to conserve and restore mountains and their related freshwater ecosystems that supply clean water, food and stable climates to over a billion people around the world.

h3.a: Kunming Biodiversity Fund, UNEP Executive Director Press Statement

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, said the Kunming Biodiversity Fund is fast-tracking finance for developing nations to scale nature action and achieve GBF goals.

h3.a: European Commission and UNEP reaffirm commitment to global environmental action and multilateralism

div.div: The agreement calls for mutual cooperation on the environment in response to today’s global challenges.

h3.a: Why a circular economy is increasingly crucial and profitable

div.div: As biodiversity plummets, circular approaches to business offer a way to conserve natural resources while still turning a profit.

h3.a: Picking up the pace on biodiversity action

div.div: UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen urged nations to accelerate transformative action, finance and cooperation to achieve biodiversity goals and halt and reverse nature loss.

h3.a: CBD COP17 Press conference, UNEP Executive Director Press Statement

div.div: UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen: COP17 must deliver a strong Yerevan Pathway through cooperation, finance and biodiversity action to implement global goals on.

h3.a: Turning ambition on nature into economic action

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, pressed on finance leaders to align public and private finance with nature, accelerate biodiversity action, reform harmful subsidies and mobilize greater investment to achieve global biodiversity goals.

h3.a: Getting the Tropical Forest Forever Facility off to a flying start

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, said the Tropical Forest Forever Facility (TFFF) is a timely financing mechanism that rewards verified forest protection, attracts large-scale investment, and supports biodiversity, climate stability, livelihoods, and ecosystem services. She called for the facility’s swift finalization, stronger financial commitments, and readiness for future investments.

h3.a: Putting private finance tools to work for biodiversity

div.div: Inger Andersen, UNEP Executive Director, says finance now recognizes nature, but biodiversity remains underfunded; governments must unlock private investment.

img.alt: A female driver drives a Transjakarta electric bus

h3.a: How women are steering Asia's shift to electric buses

div.div: From Jakarta to Hanoi, women are driving Asia's shift to electric buses—proving a UNEP-led project can cut emissions and close the transport gender gap at once.
